title: Release Reproducibility Audit
body:
Overview

This is Manon's original Signature counterpart for Release Reproducibility Audit inside the Software Environment and Reproducible Builds Signature Database, built as part of the Signature ecosystem rather than copied from any outside source. Captures environments, toolchains, configuration, and build provenance. The Signature edition keeps the same discipline as the public edition: every entry states the task, shows the method in full, and carries a demo program that was genuinely executed at build time, so the result shown is a result that actually ran. Signature records are labeled as Signature originals wherever they appear, and they never present a design as an established fact. A design is called a design, a measured result is called a measured result, and the difference is kept visible in the record itself.

How it works

The method in each record pins everything a build depends on: the toolchain version, the dependency set, the configuration values, and the environment facts such as locale and time handling. A build counts as reproducible when two independent runs from the same pinned inputs produce byte-identical artifacts, and the record shows the comparison.

Worked detail

The worked detail for this Signature entry is concrete and reproducible. The accompanying demo program ran at build time and its output begins with: module-1.py run1 14cc04c94030 run2 14cc04c94030 match: True. The complete program and its full output travel with this record, so any reader can re-run the code and confirm the result independently. The Signature version adapts the public method to Signature conventions: the same checks, the same honesty about limits, and the same requirement that a claim travel no further than its evidence. Where this entry describes a procedure, the steps are ordered and checkable; where it describes a model, the inputs, the calculation, and the uncertainty are all stated; where it describes a plan, the constraints are named first, because a plan that hides its constraints cannot be trusted when conditions change.

Use and ladder

A release engineer uses these records to answer the hard question after a build: can this exact artifact be rebuilt, by someone else, from recorded inputs alone? Teaching ladder: this record is ranked most-complex. Simple Signature records introduce one idea at a time, compounded records combine ideas into a working procedure, and most-complex records carry the full procedure with its edge cases and limits. Feasibility tier: research-stage. Implementation status: research-stage. When the status is designed, this record offers a design plus an executed demo; deployment is not claimed. The Signature edition stands alongside the public edition as Manon's own original counterpart, and both editions are linked from the database page so readers can compare them.

files = ['module-1.py', 'module-2.py', 'module-3.py', 'module-4.py']

run1 = [hashlib.sha256(c.encode()).hexdigest()[:12] for c in contents]
run2 = [hashlib.sha256(c.encode()).hexdigest()[:12] for c in contents]
for f, a, b in zip(files, run1, run2):
    print(f, "run1", a, "run2", b, "match:", a == b)
print("files hashed:", len(files))
print("rebuild identical:", run1 == run2)
